title: OpenAI to unveil 'Managed Agents' at DevDay on September 29, moving hosted-agent runtimes into the platform
subtitle: The Testing Catalog and Progressive Robot report OpenAI will let developers create Agents, Environments, and Agent Sessions directly on the OpenAI Platform, competing head-on with Anthropic Claude Code and Google's Agents SDK.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI has officially confirmed DevDay 2026 will be held on Tuesday, September 29 at Fort Mason in San Francisco, with a 10:00 AM Pacific keynote featuring Sam Altman. Reporting from The Testing Catalog on September 5 and Progressive Robot on September 7 indicates the marquee announcement will be Managed Agents — a hosted layer that lets developers create Agents, Environments, and Agent Sessions directly on the OpenAI Platform, alongside a refreshed Agents SDK for building agents that can inspect files, run commands, edit code, and operate in long-horizon sandboxed workflows.

The mechanism is the shift that matters. Until now, running a production agent on OpenAI models has meant a developer stitches together the model, a sandbox environment, a tool-use loop, state management, monitoring, and billing themselves — or pays a third-party (LangChain, LlamaIndex, an agent-focused startup) to do it. Managed Agents move that entire stack into OpenAI's platform, priced as a hosted service. That is the same architectural bet Anthropic made with Claude Code and Google is making with the Agents SDK — the frontier lab that owns the agent runtime, not just the model, captures the developer relationship.

The competitive picture matters. Anthropic's Claude Code has become the flagship developer-agent product of 2026, and Snowflake's Q2 earnings on September 2 credited its Claude-powered CoCo agent for half the beat. Google DevDay showed off Managed Agents equivalents through Gemini Enterprise on August 27, and Meta is shipping a consumer agent this month. OpenAI at DevDay on September 29 will be defending the developer surface it has held since the ChatGPT API launched, against three competitors that all now have a hosted-agent story of their own.

For learners: 'managed' is a technical word that hides a business model. When a platform managed something for you — databases, containers, now agents — it is offering to run a system that is genuinely hard to run well, in exchange for a per-hour or per-token markup and lock-in to that platform's tooling. That trade is often worth it early on, and often worth undoing later once you know exactly what you're running. Read hosted-agent announcements the way you would read a hosted-database announcement in 2012: the offer is real, and so is the lock-in.
